cues.en: This video was sponsored by Caseta by Lutron. Imagine you have a giant circuit consisting of a battery, a switch, a light bulb, and two wires which are each 300,000 kilometers long. That is the distance light travels in one second. So they would reach out halfway to the moon and then come back to be connected to the light bulb which is one meter away. Now the question is, after I close this switch, how long would it take for the bulb to light up?
cues.zh: 本视频由 Lutron 的 Caseta 赞助。想象你有一个巨大的电路，包含一个电池、一个开关、一个灯泡，以及两根各长 30 万公里的导线。这是光在一秒内传播的距离。所以导线会延伸到地月距离的一半，然后再折返回来，接在相距仅一米的灯泡上。现在的问题是：闭合开关后，灯泡需要多久才会亮起来？

cues.en: Is it half a second? One second? Two seconds? One over C seconds? Or none of the above? Now you have to make some simplifying assumptions about this circuit, like the wires have to have no resistance, otherwise this wouldn't work, and the light bulb has to turn on immediately when current passes through it. But I want you to commit to an answer and put it down in the comments so you can't say, oh yeah, I knew that was the answer when I tell you the answer later on. This question...
cues.zh: 是半秒？一秒？两秒？1/c 秒？还是以上都不是？这里需要对电路做一些理想化假设，比如导线必须没有电阻，否则根本无法工作，而且一旦有电流通过，灯泡就会瞬间点亮。但我希望你先选定一个答案写在评论区，省得待会儿公布答案时你说“啊对，我早就猜到了”。这个问题……

cues.en: actually relates to how electrical energy gets from a power plant to your home. You know, unlike a battery, the electricity in the grid comes in the form of alternating current, or AC, which means electrons in the power lines are just wiggling back and forth. They never actually go anywhere. So if the charges don't come from the power plant to your home, how does the electrical energy actually reach you?
cues.zh: 其实关系到电能是如何从发电厂输送到你家的。要知道，跟电池不同，电网里的电是交流电（AC），这意味着输电线里的电子只是在来回晃动，它们其实哪儿也没去。那么，如果电荷并没有从发电厂跑到你家，电能究竟是怎么送达的呢？

cues.en: When I used to teach this subject, I would say that power lines are like this flexible plastic tubing, and the electrons inside are like this chain. So what a power station does is it pushes and pulls the electrons back and forth 60 times a second. Now at your house, you can plug in a device like a toaster, which essentially means allowing the electrons to run through it. So when the power station pushes and pulls the electrons, well...
cues.zh: 以前教这门课时，我会说输电线就像这种塑料软管，里面的电子就像这条链子。发电站做的事情，就是以每秒 60 次的频率来回推拉这些电子。而在你家里，插上烤面包机等电器，本质上就是让电子从中穿过。所以当发电站推拉电子时，嗯……

cues.en: they encounter resistance in the toaster element, and they dissipate their energy as heat, and so you can toast your bread. Now this is a great story, I think it's easy to visualize, and I think my students understood it. The only problem is, it's wrong. For one thing, there is no continuous conducting wire that runs all the way from a power station to your house.
cues.zh: 它们在烤面包机的发热元件中遇到电阻，将能量以热能形式耗散掉，这样就能烤面包了。这个解释很棒，画面感强，我的学生也听懂了。唯一的问题是——它是错的。首先，根本就没有一根连续的导线一路从发电厂通到你家。

cues.en: No, there are physical gaps, there are breaks in the line, like in transformers, where one coil of wire is wrapped on one side, a different coil of wire is wrapped on the other side, so electrons cannot possibly flow from one to the other. Plus, I mean, if it's the electrons that are carrying the energy from the power station to your device, then when those same electrons flow back to the power station, why are they not also carrying energy back from your house
cues.zh: 并不存在，线路上有物理间隙、有断点，比如变压器（Transformer）里，一侧绕着一个线圈，另一侧绕着另一个线圈，电子根本不可能从一边流到另一边。而且，如果是电子把能量从发电站带到你的设备，那当同一批电子流回发电站时，为什么它们没有把能量从你家带回……

cues.en: to the power station. I mean, if the flow of current is two ways, then why does energy only flow in one direction? These are the lies you were taught about electricity, that electrons themselves have potential energy, that they are pushed or pulled through a continuous conducting loop, and that they dissipate their energy in the device. My claim in this video is that all of that is false.
cues.zh: 发电站呢？我的意思是，如果电流是双向流动的，为什么能量却只沿单向流动？这些都是你学过的关于电的谎言：电子本身具有势能、它们在连续闭合的导线回路中被推拉、并在用电设备中耗散能量。我在本期视频中要证明的是，所有这些说法全是错的。

cues.en: So, how does it actually work? In the 1860s and 70s, there was a huge breakthrough in our understanding of the universe. When Scottish physicist James Clerk Maxwell realized that light is made up of oscillating electric and magnetic fields. The fields are oscillating perpendicular to each other and they are in phase, meaning when one is at its maximum, so is the other wave.
cues.zh: 所以，它到底是怎么运作的？19 世纪 60 到 70 年代，我们对宇宙的理解出现了巨大突破。当时苏格兰物理学家 James Clerk Maxwell 意识到，光由振荡的电场和磁场组成。这些场彼此垂直地振荡，并且同相，也就是说，当一个场达到最大值时，另一个波也达到最大值。

cues.en: Now, he works out the equations that govern the behavior of electric and magnetic fields, and hence these waves. Those are now called Maxwell's equations. But in 1883, one of Maxwell's former students, John Henry Pointing, is thinking about conservation of energy. If energy is conserved locally in every tiny bit of space, well, then you should be able to trace the path that energy flows from one place to another.
cues.zh: 现在，他推导出支配电场和磁场行为、进而支配这些波的方程。这些现在被称为 Maxwell 方程组。但到了 1883 年，Maxwell 以前的一位学生 John Henry Pointing 在思考能量守恒。如果能量在每一小块空间中局域守恒，那么你应该能够追踪能量从一处流向另一处的路径。

cues.en: So think about the energy that comes to us from the sun. I mean, during those eight minutes when the light is traveling, the energy is stored and being transmitted in the electric and magnetic fields of the light. Now, pointing works out an equation to describe energy flux. That is, how much electromagnetic energy is passing through an area per second. This is known as the pointing vector, and it's given the symbol S.
cues.zh: 想想从太阳来到我们这里的能量。我的意思是，在光传播的那八分钟里，能量储存在光的电场和磁场中，并被传输。现在，Pointing 推导出一个描述能量通量的方程。也就是每秒钟有多少电磁能通过某个面积。这被称为坡印廷矢量，符号是 S。

cues.en: And the formula is really pretty simple. It's just a constant, 1 over mu naught, which is the permeability of free space, times E cross B. Now, E cross B is the cross product of the electric and magnetic fields. Now, the cross product is just a particular way of multiplying two vectors together.
cues.zh: 公式其实非常简单。就是一个常数，1 除以 μ₀，也就是真空磁导率，乘以 E cross B。E cross B 是电场和磁场的叉积。叉积只是两个向量相乘的一种特定方式。

cues.en: where you multiply their perpendicular magnitudes. And to find the direction, you put your fingers in the direction of the first vector, which in this case is the electric field, and curl them in the direction of the second vector, the magnetic field. Then your thumb points in the direction of the resulting vector, the energy flux. So what this shows us about light is that the energy is flowing perpendicular to both the electric and the magnetic fields. And it's in the same direction as the light is traveling.
cues.zh: 也就是把彼此垂直的分量相乘。要确定方向，你把手指指向第一个向量，这里是电场，然后向第二个向量，磁场的方向弯曲。拇指指向结果向量，也就是能量通量的方向。所以这告诉我们，光的能量垂直于电场和磁场流动。并且方向与光传播方向相同。

cues.en: So this makes a lot of sense. Light carries energy from its source out to its destination. But the kicker is this. Pointing's equation doesn't just work for light. It works any time there are electric and magnetic fields coinciding. Any time you have electric and magnetic fields together, there is a flow of energy and you can calculate it using Pointing's vector.
cues.zh: 所以这很合理。光把能量从源头带到目的地。但关键在于：坡印廷方程不只适用于光。只要电场和磁场同时存在，它就适用。只要有电场和磁场在一起，就有能量流动，你可以用坡印廷矢量计算。

cues.en: To illustrate this, let's consider a simple circuit with a battery and a light bulb. The battery by itself has an electric field, but since no charges are moving, there is no magnetic field, so the battery doesn't lose energy. When the battery is connected into the circuit, its electric field extends through the circuit at the speed of light.
cues.zh: 为了说明这一点，考虑一个带电池和灯泡的简单电路。电池本身有电场，但因为没有电荷移动，所以没有磁场，因此电池不会损失能量。当电池接入电路时，它的电场以光速延伸到整个电路。

cues.en: This electric field pushes electrons around so they accumulate on some of the surfaces of the conductors, making them negatively charged, and are depleted elsewhere, leaving their surfaces positively charged. These surface charges create a small electric field inside the wires, causing electrons to drift preferentially in one direction. Note that this drift velocity is extremely slow, around a tenth of a millimeter per second.
cues.zh: 这个电场推动电子移动，使它们聚集在导体的某些表面上，从而带负电；而其他地方的电子被耗尽，使那些表面带正电。这些表面电荷在导线内部产生一个小电场，使电子优先向一个方向漂移。注意，这种漂移速度极慢，约为每秒0.1毫米。

cues.en: But this is current. Well, conventional current is defined to flow opposite the motion of electrons, but this is what's making it happen. The charge on the surfaces of the conductors also creates an electric field outside the wires. And the current inside the wires creates a magnetic field outside the wires. So now there is a combination of electric and magnetic fields in the space around this circuit. So according to Pointing's theory,
cues.zh: 但这就是电流。嗯，常规电流的方向被定义为与电子运动方向相反，但正是这一过程在产生电流。导体表面上的电荷也会在导线外部产生电场。导线内部的电流会在导线外部产生磁场。所以现在，电路周围的空间中同时存在电场和磁场。因此，按照 Poynting 理论，

cues.en: energy should be flowing. And we can work out the direction of this energy flow using the right hand rule. Around the battery, for example, the electric field is down and the magnetic field is into the screen. So you find the energy flux is to the right, away from the battery. In fact, all around the battery, you'll find the energy is radially outwards. Energy is going out through the sides of the battery into the fields.
cues.zh: 能量应该正在流动。我们可以用右手定则确定这种能量流动的方向。例如在电池周围，电场向下，磁场指向屏幕内。于是你会发现能量通量向右，远离电池。事实上，在电池四周，能量都沿径向向外。能量通过电池的侧面流出，进入场中。

cues.en: Along the wires, again, you can use the right hand rule to find the energy is flowing to the right. This is true for the fields along the top wire and the bottom wire. But at the filament, the pointing vector is directed in toward the light bulb. So the light bulb is getting energy from the field. If you do the cross product, you find the energy is coming in from all around the bulb.
cues.zh: 沿着导线，同样可以用右手定则发现能量向右流动。上方导线和下方导线沿线的场都是如此。但在灯丝处，Poynting 矢量指向灯泡内部。所以灯泡从场中获得能量。如果做叉积，你会发现能量从灯泡四周流入。

cues.en: It takes many paths from the battery to the bulb, but in all cases, the energy is transmitted by the electric and magnetic fields. People seem to think that you're pumping electrons and that you're like buying electrons or something, which is just so wrong. For most people, and I think to this day, it's quite counterintuitive to think that the energy is flowing through the space around the conductor. But the energy, which is traveling through the field, yeah, is going quite fast.
cues.zh: 从电池到灯泡有许多路径，但在所有情况下，能量都由电场和磁场传输。人们似乎以为你是在泵电子，或者像是在买电子之类的，这完全是错的。对大多数人来说，而且我认为直到今天，认为能量通过导体周围的空间流动仍然相当反直觉。但能量确实通过场传播，而且速度相当快。

cues.en: So, there are a few things to notice here. Even though the electrons go two ways, away from the battery and towards it, by using the pointing vector, you find that the energy flux only goes one way, from the battery to the bulb. This also shows it's the fields and not the electrons that carry the energy. I mean, how far do the electrons go in this little thing you're talking about? They barely move. They probably don't move at all.
cues.zh: 这里要注意几点。即使电子会往两个方向运动，远离电池和流向电池，用 Poynting 矢量你会发现能量通量只朝一个方向，从电池到灯泡。这也说明携带能量的是场，而不是电子。我的意思是，在你说的这个小装置里，电子到底能走多远？它们几乎不动。它们可能根本不动。

cues.en: Now what happens if in place of a battery we use an alternating current source? Well then the direction of current reverses every half cycle. But this means that both the electric and magnetic fields flip at the same time. So at any instant the pointing vector still points in the same direction from the source to the bulb. So the exact same analysis we used for DC still works for AC.
cues.zh: 那如果把电池换成交流电源，会发生什么？这时电流方向每半个周期反转一次。但这意味着电场和磁场会同时翻转。所以在任意时刻，坡印廷矢量仍然从电源指向灯泡，方向不变。因此，我们用于直流电的同一套分析，对交流电仍然成立。

cues.en: And this explains how energy is able to flow from power plants to homes in power lines. Inside the wires, electrons just oscillate back and forth. Their motion is greatly exaggerated here. But they do not carry the energy. Outside the wires, oscillating electric and magnetic fields travel from the power station to your home. You can use the pointing vector to check that the energy flux is going in one direction.
cues.zh: 这就解释了能量如何通过输电线从发电厂流向家庭。在导线内部，电子只是来回振荡。这里把它们的运动大大夸张了。但电子并不携带能量。在导线外部，振荡的电场和磁场从发电站传播到你家。你可以用坡印廷矢量来验证能流是朝一个方向进行的。

cues.en: You might think this is just an academic discussion, that you could see the energy as transmitted either by fields or by the current in the wire. But that is not the case. And people learned this the hard way when they started laying undersea telegraph cables. The first transatlantic cable was laid in 1858. It only worked for about a month. It never worked properly. There are all kinds of distortions when they try to send enormous amounts of distortion.
cues.zh: 你可能觉得这只是学术讨论：能量既可以看作由场传输，也可以看作由导线中的电流传输。但事实并非如此。人们在开始铺设海底电报电缆时，才痛苦地认识到这一点。第一条跨大西洋电缆于1858年铺设。它只正常工作了一个月左右。它从未真正稳定运行过。当他们试图发送大量信号时，会出现各种失真。

cues.en: They can work it at a few words per minute. What they found was sending signals over such a long distance under the sea, the pulses became distorted and lengthened. It was hard to differentiate dots from dashes. To account for the failure, there was a debate among scientists. William Thompson, the future Lord Kelvin, thought electrical signals moved through submarine cables like water flowing through a rubber tube.
cues.zh: 它只能以每分钟几个词的速度工作。他们发现，在海底如此长的距离上发送信号时，脉冲会失真并被拉长。很难区分点和划。为了解释这次失败，科学家之间展开了争论。William Thompson，也就是后来的 Lord Kelvin，认为电信号通过海底电缆传输，就像水在橡胶管中流动。

cues.en: But others, like Heveside and Fitzgerald, argued it was the fields around the wires that carried the energy and information. And ultimately, this view proved correct. To insulate and protect the submarine cable, the central copper conductor had been coated in an insulator and then encased in an iron sheath. The iron was only meant to strengthen the cable,
cues.zh: 但 Heveside 和 Fitzgerald 等人认为，携带能量和信息的是导线周围的场。最终，这种观点被证明是正确的。为了给海底电缆绝缘并提供保护，中心的铜导体先涂上绝缘层，然后包在铁护套里。铁原本只是为了加固电缆，

cues.en: But as a good conductor, it interfered with the propagation of electromagnetic fields because it increased the capacitance of the line. This is why today most power lines are suspended high up. Even the damp earth acts as a conductor, so you want a large insulating gap of air to separate the wires from the ground. So what is the answer to our giant circuit light bulb question? Well, after I close the switch, the light bulb will turn on...
cues.zh: 但铁是良导体，会增加线路的电容，从而干扰电磁场的传播。这就是为什么今天大多数输电线都架得很高。即使潮湿的土壤也会充当导体，所以你需要用一大段空气绝缘间隙把导线和地面隔开。那么，我们那个巨型电路灯泡问题的答案是什么？在我合上开关后，灯泡会亮起……

cues.en: almost instantaneously in roughly 1 over C seconds. So the correct answer is D. I think a lot of people imagine that the electric field needs to travel from the battery all the way down the wire, which is a light second long, so it should take a second for the bulb to light up. But what we've learned in this video is it's not really what's happening in the wires that matters. It's what happens around the wires.
cues.zh: 几乎瞬间亮起，大约在 1/c 秒内。所以正确答案是 D。我想很多人会以为，电场需要从电池一路沿导线传播，而导线有一光秒长，所以灯泡应该要一秒才亮。但我们在本视频中学到的是，真正重要的并不是导线内部发生了什么，而是导线周围发生了什么。

cues.en: and the electric and magnetic fields can propagate out through space to this light bulb which is only one meter away in a few nanoseconds. And so that is the limiting factor for the light bulb turning on. Now the bulb won't receive the entire voltage of the battery immediately, it'll be some fraction which depends on the impedance of these lines and the impedance of the bulb. Now I asked several experts about this question and got
cues.zh: 电场和磁场能在几纳秒内穿过空间，传播到仅一米外的这个灯泡。所以这就是灯泡亮起的限制因素。现在灯泡不会立刻获得电池的全部电压，而只会得到一部分，这取决于这些线路的阻抗和灯泡的阻抗。现在我就这个问题问了几位专家，得到了

cues.en: kind of different answers, but we all agreed on these main points. So I'm going to put their analysis in the description in case you want to learn more about this particular setup. If I get called out on it and people don't think it's real, we can definitely invest the resources and string up some lines and make our own power lines in the desert. I think you're going to get called out on it. I agree. I think you're going to get called out. I think that's right.
cues.zh: 一些不同的答案，但我们在这些主要观点上意见一致。所以我会把他们的分析放在简介里，以防你想更深入了解这个特定装置。如果我因此被质疑，而且人们觉得这不真实，我们完全可以投入资源，拉几条线，在沙漠里搭我们自己的电力线。我觉得你会因此被质疑。我同意。我觉得你会被质疑。我觉得没错。

cues.en: I think it's just kind of wild that this is one of those things that we use every day that almost nobody thinks about or knows the right answer to. These traveling electromagnetic waves around power lines are really what's delivering your power.
cues.zh: 我觉得有点不可思议：这是我们每天都在用的东西，却几乎没人会去想，也没人知道正确答案。电线周围这些行进的电磁波，才是真正把电能送到你家的东西。

cues.en: Hey, now that you understand how electrical energy actually flows, you can think about that every time you flick on a light switch. And if you want to take your switches to the next level, the sponsor of this video, Caseta by Lutron, provides premium smart lighting control, including switches, remotes, and plug-in smart dimmers. And since one switch can control many regular bulbs, you can effectively make all those bulbs smart.

And once you're already in bed, you can check which lights you forgot to turn off and do that from your phone. Installation is easy. cues.zh: 这个功能让你安心：家里每个人回家时，房子总是亮着灯。而当你已经躺在床上时，还能查看自己忘了关哪些灯，并用手机把它们关掉。安装很简单。先确保切断开关的电源，然后断开现有电线，接上 Caseta 的智能开关。如果你需要帮助，点一下或打个电话就能联系到他们。想了解更多关于 Caseta 的信息，请访问 Lutron 网站 lutron.com/veritasium。我会把链接放在简介里。
